about: Estate and inheritance taxes in force: the federal estate tax and the twelve states and D.C. with an estate tax, the five states with an inheritance tax. An estate tax is on the estate above its exemption, at a rate that rises from the low rate to the top rate across the taxable amount (slideOver, dollars above the exemption). An inheritance tax is on each heir's share above the exemption for their relation to the decedent, at that relation's rate; relations not listed fall in 'others'. Dollars, not cents.
source: Tax Foundation, 'Estate and Inheritance Taxes by State, 2026' (rates and exemptions as of October 1, 2026), https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/estate-inheritance-taxes/
slideOverNote: Where a state's schedule runs from a low to a high rate, the top rate is reached at $10,040,000 of taxable estate, the top bracket of the former federal state death tax credit table (26 U.S.C. 2011(b), before 2005) that Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Rhode Island and others still follow. Applied to every graduated state schedule as an estimate.

federal.source: IRS Rev. Proc. 2024-40, section 3.41 (2025 basic exclusion amount $13,990,000); 26 U.S.C. 2001(c) and 2010: with the unified credit, every dollar above the exclusion is taxed at the 40 percent top rate.
Public Law 119-21 (2025), section 70106: basic exclusion amount $15,000,000 from 2026, indexed for inflation after; Tax Foundation 2026 table.

estateEstimateNote: The 2026 table's exemptions and rates are applied from the game's opening in 2025; indexed exemptions (Connecticut, New York, Rhode Island, D.C., Maine) were a few percent lower in 2025.

US-KY.source: Ky. Rev. Stat. 140.070 and 140.080: Class A (spouse, parent, child, grandchild, brother, sister) exempt; Class C 6 to 16 percent above $500, the top rate over $200,000.

US-MD.source: Md. Code, Tax-General 7-203: spouse, children, parents, grandparents, grandchildren and siblings exempt; others 10 percent.

US-NE.source: Neb. Rev. Stat. 77-2004 to 77-2006 as amended by LB 310 (2022): spouse exempt; immediate relatives 1 percent above $100,000; others 15 percent above $25,000 (remote relatives, 11 percent above $40,000, are not a relation the game records).

US-NJ.source: N.J.S.A. 54:34-2: Class A (spouse, parents, grandparents, children, grandchildren) exempt; Class C (siblings) 11 percent above $25,000 rising to 16 percent above $1,700,000; Class D 15 percent, 16 percent above $700,000.

US-PA.source: 72 P.S. 9116: spouse 0 percent; lineal heirs 4.5 percent; siblings 12 percent; others 15 percent (a parent inheriting from a child 21 or younger pays 0, not modeled).
